Security backport for zstd 0.13.3: RUSTSEC-2026-0391

Upstream crate: https://crates.io/crates/zstd/0.13.3
Upstream fix: https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/74ace2dcdca62a2ce0f034895d6079458311e003
License: MIT, retained in LICENSE. This local copy is not publishable.

Polars 0.55.2 still requires zstd 0.13 and uses Decoder::with_context while
reading Parquet pages. Reusing an abandoned context without resetting its
session can expose data from the previous job or corrupt the next stream.
Backport the upstream SessionOnly resets in both borrowed-context constructors.
Do not alter parameters, dictionary contents or compression formats.

Extended binding qualification (2026-10-27): select upstream zstd-safe 8.2.0
and its fixed zstd-sys >=2.1.2 while keeping this compatible 0.13 wrapper.
Both packages originate at upstream commit
75bc74045a2f6ea0439aeed7e159a266da20aac0. The fixed bindings address the old
legacy-error output positions, dictionary/context lifetime, experimental-buffer
and seekable/allocator advisories instead of locally reimplementing unsafe FFI.
The same six explicit prepared-dictionary owner lifetimes used by upstream
zstd 0.14.3 are carried through raw, read and write constructors. This deliberately
rejects code that drops a prepared dictionary before its stream; dictionary
bytes alone do not keep the C dictionary allocation alive. Safe owned-lifetime
dictionary use and all existing codecs remain supported.

The reserved-bit legacy frame regression reported 1024 bytes of output from an
unsuccessful call before the binding update. The added tests verify zero output
and consumed positions on failure, no stale writer output after flush/drop,
prepared-dictionary round trips and compile-time owner lifetime rejection.

The added encoder and decoder isolation tests fail on the unmodified crate and
pass with this patch. Run the complete upstream suite and these regressions with:
  cargo test --manifest-path aq-engine/vendor/zstd/Cargo.toml --offline
The test crate has an isolated workspace and tracked qualification lockfile;
its target directory remains ignored.
The CLI/legacy binary fixtures omitted by crates.io are restored from original
source commit 52e9d41a645fb49edcf1ed3df765f380dbcf13b2. The long-source test uses
the included text repeated to 242 KiB instead of an absent sibling bindings file.

Both the AQS workspace and standalone AQE source manifests select this patch.
Cargo patches are not inherited by downstream crates.io consumers. Publishing
AQE or claiming the registry dependency is fixed therefore remains gated on an
upstream compatible release/dependency update or an explicit reviewed downstream
patch. Do not remove this patch merely to make an audit count look smaller.
The root and isolated qualification lockfiles must select fixed zstd-safe and
zstd-sys versions. Audit that graph separately: local wrapper source paths are
not registry-advisory evidence. Native/WASM/research and feature qualification
is recorded in the security review; a source build is not deployment proof.

Remove the local copy once the dependency graph accepts an upstream fixed codec
and these tests plus Parquet round trips pass on that graph.
